Kemecse Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kemecse, Hungary

Not demolished. Kemecse's Jewish community formed around 1820, founded by Jewish farmers who settled in the village; its first rabbi was Gerson Grünwald, and a synagogue was built in 1824. The cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1828, its newest to 1944. The community supported a yeshiva with about 25 students under Talmud Torah head Arnold Láng, and its members were prominent locally: Jenő Roth led the town's Savings Bank, Ignác Haas farmed 1,200 acres and ran a mill and distillery, and the Ehrenberg and Zwibel families operated oil refineries that employed many villagers. Of 32 community members who served in World War I, 5 died. By 1944 the Orthodox community had grown to 316 members, with its Talmud Torah run by two teachers.
